people.adam.meaning: His name opens the book. The list gives only his name, then Seth and Enosh.
people.enoch.meaning: The list names him between Jared and Methuselah. It tells no story about him.
people.noah.meaning: The list names him after Lamech. It then names Shem, Ham, and Japheth and follows their families.
people.shem.role: Noah’s son and ancestor of Abraham
people.shem.relations: Brother of Ham and Japheth. Ancestor of Abraham.
people.shem.meaning: The list names his sons, starting with Elam and Asshur. It then runs from Shem through Arpachshad and Eber to Abram.
people.ham.meaning: His sons are Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan. The list names Nimrod, the Jebusite, and the Amorite in this branch.
people.japheth.meaning: His seven sons come first in the list, starting with Gomer. The list then names the sons of Gomer and Javan. It tells no story about him.
people.nimrod.meaning: Cush is his father. The list says he began to be a mighty one on the earth. It says no more about him.
people.abraham.meaning: The list calls him Abram, also called Abraham. It names his sons Isaac and Ishmael, then the sons of Keturah. David’s song recalls the covenant God made with him. David’s last prayer calls the LORD the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.
people.ishmael.meaning: He is a son of Abraham. The list names his twelve sons, from Nebaioth to Kedemah. It then turns to Keturah’s sons and to Isaac.
people.isaac.role: Abraham’s son, named in the list and in praise
people.isaac.meaning: He is Abraham’s son, and his sons are Esau and Israel. David’s song recalls God’s oath to Isaac. David’s last prayer names him with Abraham and Israel.
people.esau.meaning: He is Isaac’s son. The list names his five sons and their sons. It then lists the kings and chiefs of Edom.
people.jacob.meaning: The family list calls him Israel and names his twelve sons. David’s song calls the people children of Jacob. It says God confirmed the covenant to Jacob. David’s last prayer names Israel with Abraham and Isaac.
people.keturah.relations: Abraham’s concubine. Mother of six sons named here.
people.keturah.meaning: She bears six sons, from Zimran to Shuah. The list also names the sons of Jokshan and Midian. It tells no story about her.
people.judah.meaning: He has five sons. Shua’s daughter bears three, and Tamar bears Perez and Zerah. The LORD kills his firstborn, Er, who was wicked. Chapter 5 says Judah prevailed above his brothers, and the prince came from him.
people.tamar.meaning: She is Judah’s daughter-in-law. She bears him Perez and Zerah. The line to David runs through Perez and Hezron.
people.boaz.meaning: The list names him as Salma’s son and Obed’s father. It tells no story about him.
people.obed.meaning: He is the son of Boaz and the father of Jesse. The list tells no story about him.
people.jesse.relations: Son of Obed. Father of seven sons and of Zeruiah and Abigail.
people.jesse.meaning: He has seven sons. Eliab is the firstborn, and David is the seventh. Later chapters call David the son of Jesse.
people.david.role: King who brings the ark and prepares the temple
people.david.meaning: All Israel anoints David king at Hebron, and he takes Jerusalem. He brings the ark there and sets Levites to sing before it. God tells him that his son will build the temple. David counts Israel, buys Ornan’s threshing floor, and gathers gold, stone, and cedar. He gives Solomon the plans and dies at a good old age.
people.zeruiah.meaning: The list names her as a sister of Jesse’s sons. Her sons are Abishai, Joab, and Asahel. Later chapters call Joab and Abishai sons of Zeruiah. The book tells no story about her.
people.abigail-sister.relations: Daughter of Jesse. Sister of David and Zeruiah. Mother of Amasa.
people.abigail-sister.meaning: She is a sister of David and Zeruiah. She bears Amasa to Jether the Ishmaelite. David’s wife Abigail the Carmelitess is another woman.
people.joab.role: Army chief who objects to David’s count
people.joab.meaning: He goes up first against the Jebusites, and David makes him chief. He defeats the Syrians and later strikes Rabbah. He objects when David orders the count. He counts Israel but leaves out Levi and Benjamin.
people.abishai.meaning: He lifts his spear against three hundred and kills them. He is made captain of the three. He strikes eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. The children of Ammon flee before him when Joab defeats the Syrians.
people.asahel.role: David’s nephew among the mighty men
people.asahel.meaning: He is one of Zeruiah’s three sons. The list of mighty men names him in 11:26. He leads the army division for the fourth month. His son Zebadiah leads it after him.
people.amasa.relations: Son of Abigail and Jether the Ishmaelite. Nephew of David.
people.amasa.meaning: Abigail bears him to Jether the Ishmaelite. The list tells no story about him.
people.caleb-hezron.meaning: He has children by Azubah and by Jerioth. After Azubah dies he marries Ephrath, who bears Hur. Hur’s grandson is Bezalel. A second list names more sons, two concubines, and his daughter Achsah. Chapter 4 names a Caleb who is Jephunneh’s son.
people.jarha.role: Egyptian servant who marries Sheshan’s daughter
people.jarha.meaning: He is an Egyptian servant of Sheshan. Sheshan has no sons, so he gives Jarha his daughter as wife. She bears Attai. The list follows their family from Attai down to Elishama.
people.amnon.meaning: He is David’s firstborn, born at Hebron. His mother is Ahinoam the Jezreelitess. The list tells no story about him.
people.abigail.relations: Called the Carmelitess. Wife of David and mother of Daniel.
people.abigail.meaning: The list calls her Abigail the Carmelitess. She bears Daniel, David’s second son, at Hebron. David’s sister Abigail in chapter 2 is another woman.
people.ahinoam-david.relations: Called the Jezreelitess. Mother of David’s firstborn, Amnon.
people.ahinoam-david.meaning: The list calls her Ahinoam the Jezreelitess. She bears Amnon, David’s firstborn, at Hebron. The list tells no story about her.
people.absalom.meaning: He is David’s third son, born at Hebron. His mother is Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. The list tells no story about him.
people.adonijah.meaning: He is David’s fourth son, born at Hebron. His mother is Haggith. The list tells no story about him.
people.bathsheba.meaning: The list calls her Bathshua, the daughter of Ammiel. She bears David four sons in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon. The book of Samuel words her name and family differently.
people.solomon.role: David’s son chosen to build the temple
people.solomon.meaning: He is born in Jerusalem to David and Bathshua. David tells him to build the LORD’s house and gives him the plans. The assembly anoints him, and he sits on the throne. All Israel obeys him.
people.tamar-david.role: David’s daughter listed after his sons
people.tamar-david.meaning: The list names her after David’s sons as their sister. It tells no story about her. Judah’s daughter-in-law Tamar in chapter 2 is another woman.
people.rehoboam.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.rehoboam.relations: Son of Solomon and Naamah. Father of Abijah.
people.rehoboam.meaning: The list names him as Solomon’s son and Abijah’s father. It tells no story about him.
people.asa.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.asa.relations: Son of Abijah. Father of Jehoshaphat.
people.asa.meaning: The list places him between Abijah and Jehoshaphat. It tells no story about him.
people.jehoshaphat.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.jehoshaphat.meaning: The list places him between Asa and Joram. It tells no story about him.
people.jehoram-judah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.jehoram-judah.relations: Son of Jehoshaphat. Father of Ahaziah.
people.jehoram-judah.meaning: The list calls him Joram. It places him between Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah. It tells no story about him.
people.ahaziah-judah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.ahaziah-judah.meaning: The list places him between Joram and Joash. It tells no story about him.
people.joash-judah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.joash-judah.meaning: The list places him between Ahaziah and Amaziah. It tells no story about him.
people.amaziah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.amaziah.meaning: The list places him between Joash and Azariah. It tells no story about him.
people.azariah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.azariah.meaning: The list calls him Azariah. It places him between Amaziah and Jotham. Second Chronicles also uses the name Uzziah.
people.jotham.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.jotham.relations: Son of Azariah. Father of Ahaz.
people.jotham.meaning: The list places him between Azariah and Ahaz. Chapter 5 says the families of Gad were listed in his days.
people.ahaz.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.ahaz.meaning: The list places him between Jotham and Hezekiah. It tells no story about him.
people.hezekiah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.hezekiah.meaning: The list places him between Ahaz and Manasseh. In his days, men of Simeon take pasture land near Gedor (chapter 4).
people.manasseh-king.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.manasseh-king.meaning: The list places him between Hezekiah and Amon. It tells no story about him.
people.amon-king.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.amon-king.meaning: The list places him between Manasseh and Josiah. It tells no story about him.
people.josiah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.josiah.relations: Son of Amon and Jedidah. Father of Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum.
people.josiah.meaning: He is Amon’s son. The list names his four sons: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum. From here the list follows Jehoiakim’s family.
people.jehoiakim.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.jehoiakim.meaning: He is Josiah’s second son. The list names Jeconiah and Zedekiah under him. It follows Jeconiah’s sons next.
people.jehoiachin.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.jehoiachin.meaning: The list calls him Jeconiah, the captive. It names his sons, starting with Shealtiel. The family line runs on through Pedaiah and Zerubbabel.
people.zedekiah.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.zedekiah.meaning: He is the third son of Josiah in the list. It tells no story about him. Verse 16 names another Zedekiah after Jeconiah.
people.zedekiah-jeconiah.relations: Listed after Jeconiah among the sons of Jehoiakim in 3:16.
people.zedekiah-jeconiah.meaning: Verse 16 lists him after Jeconiah, under the sons of Jehoiakim. The list tells no story about him. Verse 15 names a Zedekiah among Josiah’s sons.
people.zerubbabel.meaning: The list names him as a son of Pedaiah. His children include Meshullam, Hananiah, and their sister Shelomith. Ezra calls him Shealtiel’s son.
people.shelomith-daughter.role: Zerubbabel’s daughter in the royal list
people.shelomith-daughter.relations: Daughter of Zerubbabel. Sister of Meshullam and Hananiah.
people.shelomith-daughter.meaning: The list names her as the sister of Meshullam and Hananiah. It tells no story about her.
people.jabez.role: Man whose prayer breaks into the family list
people.jabez.relations: His mother names him. She says she bore him with sorrow.
people.jabez.meaning: He is more honorable than his brothers. He asks God to bless him and enlarge his border. He asks God to keep him from evil. God grants what he asks.
people.bithiah.meaning: She is a daughter of Pharaoh, and Mered takes her as wife. Verse 18 speaks of her sons. It is not clear which names are hers.
people.caleb.role: Son of Jephunneh who receives Hebron’s fields
people.caleb.relations: Son of Jephunneh. Father of Iru, Elah, and Naam.
people.caleb.meaning: His sons are Iru, Elah, and Naam. In chapter 6 he receives the fields and villages of Hebron. The sons of Aaron receive the city and its pasture lands. Chapter 2 names a Caleb who is Hezron’s son.
people.simeon.role: Son of Israel whose tribe lives near Beersheba
people.simeon.relations: Son of Israel. Father of Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
people.simeon.meaning: His sons are Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul. His families live at Beersheba, Ziklag, and other towns until David’s reign. They do not grow like the children of Judah. Later some take pasture near Gedor, and five hundred go to Mount Seir.
people.reuben.meaning: He is Israel’s firstborn. He defiles his father’s couch, so his birthright goes to Joseph’s sons. His sons are Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. His families live east of Gilead until Assyria carries them away.
people.joseph.meaning: He is a son of Israel. Reuben loses the birthright, and it goes to Joseph’s sons. The prince still comes from Judah.
people.beerah.relations: Son of Baal in the line of Joel.
people.beerah.meaning: He is prince of the Reubenites. Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria carries him away captive.
people.pul.relations: Verse 26 names both Pul and Tilgath Pilneser as king of Assyria.
people.pul.meaning: Verse 6 says Tilgath Pilneser carries away Beerah, prince of the Reubenites. In verse 26 God stirs up Pul and Tilgath Pilneser. He carries away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. He brings them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan.
people.jeroboam-ii.meaning: Verse 17 names him as king of Israel beside Jotham king of Judah. The families of Gad were listed in their days. The chapter tells no story about him.
people.levi.relations: Son of Israel. Father of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
people.levi.meaning: His sons are Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Chapter 6 traces priests, singers, and towns from these three. In chapter 23 David divides the Levites by the same three families.
people.aaron.role: Priest whose sons serve at the altar
people.aaron.meaning: He is a son of Amram, and he has four sons. He and his sons offer on the altar and make atonement for Israel. He is set apart to burn incense and to bless in the LORD’s name. David divides his sons’ families for service by lot.
people.moses.role: Servant of God whose commands guide worship
people.moses.meaning: He is a son of Amram and the brother of Aaron. The Levites carry the ark on poles, as Moses commanded. The tabernacle he made in the wilderness stands at Gibeon. David tells Solomon to keep the statutes the LORD gave Moses. His sons Gershom and Eliezer are counted with the tribe of Levi.
people.miriam.relations: Daughter of Amram. Sister of Aaron and Moses.
people.miriam.meaning: The list names her with Aaron and Moses as a child of Amram. It tells no story about her.
people.nadab.relations: Son of Aaron. Brother of Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
people.nadab.meaning: He is the first of Aaron’s four sons in the list. He and Abihu die before their father and have no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests.
people.abihu.meaning: He is the second of Aaron’s four sons in the list. He and Nadab die before their father and have no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests.
people.eleazar.role: Aaron’s son whose family supplies sixteen priest groups
people.eleazar.meaning: He is Aaron’s third son and the father of Phinehas. Chapter 6 traces the priests from him down to Jehozadak. He serves as priest with Ithamar after Nadab and Abihu die. His family supplies sixteen of the twenty-four groups of priests.
people.ithamar.role: Aaron’s son whose family supplies eight priest groups
people.ithamar.meaning: He is Aaron’s fourth son. He serves as priest with Eleazar after Nadab and Abihu die. His family has eight heads of houses, and Eleazar’s has sixteen. Ahimelech is one of his sons’ line.
people.phinehas.role: Priest who once ruled the gatekeepers
people.phinehas.meaning: He is the son of Eleazar and the father of Abishua. In time past he ruled over the keepers of the entry. Chapter 9 says the LORD was with him.
people.samuel.role: Seer named in family lists and records
people.samuel.meaning: Chapter 6 names his sons Joel and Abijah. Heman the singer is his grandson. He and David set the gatekeepers in their office of trust. He dedicated gifts that Shelomoth keeps. A history of Samuel the seer records David’s acts.
people.heman-singer.role: Lead singer and the king’s seer
people.heman-singer.meaning: He is a Kohathite singer and the grandson of Samuel. The Levites choose him to sound bronze cymbals when the ark moves. He then serves at Gibeon with Jeduthun, with trumpets and cymbals. He is the king’s seer, and his fourteen sons serve in song.
people.asaph-singer.role: Chief of those who give thanks before the ark
people.asaph-singer.relations: Son of Berechiah. Father of Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah.
people.asaph-singer.meaning: He stands at Heman’s right hand. He sounds cymbals when the ark moves. David makes him chief of the Levites who give thanks before the ark. David leaves him there for each day’s work. His sons later serve under him with harps and cymbals.
people.ethan-singer.meaning: He is of the sons of Merari and stands at Heman’s left hand. The Levites choose him with Heman and Asaph. He sounds bronze cymbals when the ark moves.
people.jehozadak.meaning: He is the son of Seraiah, last in the list of priests. He goes into captivity when the LORD carries away Judah and Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar is the one who takes them.
people.ephraim.role: Ancestor who mourns his killed sons
people.ephraim.meaning: Men of Gath kill his sons Ezer and Elead in a fight over livestock. He mourns many days, and his brothers come to comfort him. His wife then bears a son, and he names him Beriah. The list then names Sheerah, who builds three towns.
people.manasseh.meaning: His concubine the Aramitess bears Asriel and Machir. Machir is the father of Gilead. The list also names Zelophehad, who has daughters.
people.zelophehad.relations: Named in Machir’s family. He has daughters.
people.zelophehad.meaning: The list names him in Machir’s family. It says only that he had daughters.
people.sheerah.meaning: She builds Beth Horon the lower and the upper. She also builds Uzzen Sheerah.
people.joshua.role: Son of Nun in Ephraim’s family list
people.joshua.meaning: He is the son of Nun. His name ends a line that runs from Rephah through Elishama and Nun. The list tells no story about him.
people.serah.meaning: She is the sister of Asher’s four sons. The list tells no story about her.
people.benjamin.meaning: He is the father of Bela, Ashbel, Aharah, Nohah, and Rapha. The chapter names his families in Geba, Aijalon, Gibeon, and Jerusalem. It ends with Saul’s family.
people.saul.meaning: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa and kill his sons. Archers overtake Saul, and he falls on his sword. The chapter says he died because he did not keep the LORD’s word. The LORD turns the kingdom over to David.
people.jonathan-saul.role: Saul’s son who dies on Mount Gilboa
people.jonathan-saul.meaning: The family list names him first among Saul’s sons. His son is Merib-baal. The Philistines kill him with his brothers Abinadab and Malchishua on Mount Gilboa. David’s nephew Jonathan in chapter 20 is another man.
people.mephibosheth-jonathan.role: Merib-baal, Jonathan’s son in Saul’s family
people.mephibosheth-jonathan.relations: Son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul. Father of Micah.
people.mephibosheth-jonathan.meaning: The list calls him Merib-baal. He is Jonathan’s son and the father of Micah. Samuel calls him Mephibosheth. The list tells no story about him.
people.ishbosheth.relations: Son of Saul. Brother of Jonathan, Malchishua, and Abinadab.
people.ishbosheth.meaning: The list calls him Eshbaal. He is the last of Saul’s four sons in the list. Samuel tells about his rule after Saul’s death.
people.shallum-gatekeeper.meaning: He is chief of the gatekeepers. He and his Korahite brothers keep the thresholds of the tent. Their fathers kept the entry of the LORD’s camp. Verse 31 names Mattithiah as the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite.
people.mattithiah-baker.role: Levite over things baked in pans
people.mattithiah-baker.meaning: He is a Levite and the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite. He has the office of trust over the things baked in pans.
people.saul-armor-bearer.meaning: Saul asks him to draw his sword and kill him. He will not, for he is terrified. Saul falls on his own sword. When he sees that Saul is dead, he falls on his sword and dies.
people.jashobeam.meaning: He is chief of the thirty. He lifts his spear against three hundred and kills them at one time. He leads the army division for the first month. A Korahite named Jashobeam joins David at Ziklag, perhaps another man.
people.eleazar-dodai.relations: Son of Dodo the Ahohite. One of the three mighty men.
people.eleazar-dodai.meaning: He is with David at Pasdammim when the people flee from the Philistines. They stand in a plot of barley and defend it. They kill the Philistines, and the LORD saves them by a great victory.
people.benaiah.meaning: He kills the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He kills a lion in a pit on a snowy day. He takes a tall Egyptian’s spear and kills him with it. David sets him over his guard, and he leads the third month’s division.
people.uriah.meaning: The list of mighty men names Uriah the Hittite. It tells no story about him. Samuel tells how David ordered his death.
people.amasai-warrior.role: Chief of the thirty who pledges peace
people.amasai-warrior.relations: Chief of the thirty. He speaks for men of Benjamin and Judah.
people.amasai-warrior.meaning: Men of Benjamin and Judah come to David’s stronghold. David asks if they come to help or to betray him. The Spirit comes on Amasai, and he says, “We are yours, David.” David receives them and makes them captains.
people.zadok.role: Priest who serves under David and Solomon
people.zadok.meaning: A young warrior named Zadok comes to David at Hebron with twenty-two captains. David calls Zadok the priest and Abiathar to bring up the ark. Zadok then offers burnt offerings at Gibeon. He helps David divide the priests by lot. The assembly anoints him priest when Solomon is made king.
people.abinadab-ark.role: Man whose house holds the ark
people.abinadab-ark.relations: The ark is in his house. Uzza and Ahio drive the cart from there.
people.abinadab-ark.meaning: The ark is in his house at Kiriath Jearim. David and all Israel bring it out on a new cart. The chapter tells nothing more about him.
people.uzzah.relations: He drives the cart with Ahio from Abinadab’s house.
people.uzzah.meaning: He and Ahio drive the cart that carries the ark. The oxen stumble at Chidon’s threshing floor. Uzza puts out his hand to hold the ark. The LORD strikes him, and he dies there. David is afraid and leaves the ark with Obed-Edom.
people.ahio.role: Man who drives the ark cart with Uzza
people.ahio.relations: He drives the cart with Uzza from Abinadab’s house.
people.ahio.meaning: He and Uzza drive the new cart from Abinadab’s house. The chapter says nothing more about him.
people.obed-edom.role: Gittite whose house keeps the ark
people.obed-edom.meaning: David carries the ark aside into his house. It stays three months, and the LORD blesses his house. David later brings the ark up from his house with joy. Chapter 15 also names an Obed-Edom among the doorkeepers and harp players.
people.hiram.role: King of Tyre who sends cedar and workers
people.hiram.relations: King of Tyre. He sends messengers to David.
people.hiram.meaning: He sends messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters. They are to build David a house. David then sees that the LORD has made him king.
people.abiathar.role: Priest David calls to move the ark
people.abiathar.relations: Priest named with Zadok. Father of Ahimelech in 24:6.
people.abiathar.meaning: David calls Abiathar and Zadok to make ready and bring up the ark. Chapter 27 names him after Ahithophel, the king’s counselor.
people.chenaniah-music.relations: Chief of the Levites. He teaches the singers.
people.chenaniah-music.meaning: He is over the singing when the ark comes up. He teaches the singers because he is skillful. He wears fine linen with the singers and the Levites. Other translations word his task differently.
people.michal.relations: Daughter of Saul. Wife of David.
people.michal.meaning: She looks out a window as the ark comes into David’s city. She sees King David dancing and playing. She despises him in her heart.
people.jeduthun.role: Musician who gives thanks with the harp
people.jeduthun.relations: Father of sons who serve in music and at the gate.
people.jeduthun.meaning: He serves at Gibeon with Heman, giving thanks with trumpets and cymbals. His sons are at the gate. Later his sons serve under him in the LORD’s house. He prophesies with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
people.obed-edom-jeduthun.meaning: David leaves him and Hosah as doorkeepers before the ark. The same verse names an Obed-Edom with sixty-eight relatives. The text does not say if they are one man.
people.hosah.meaning: David leaves him as a doorkeeper before the ark. He is of the children of Merari. He makes Shimri chief, though Shimri is not the firstborn. The lot gives him and Shuppim the west gate.
people.nathan-prophet.role: Prophet who brings God’s answer to David
people.nathan-prophet.relations: Prophet who speaks with David. A history of David’s acts bears his name.
people.nathan-prophet.meaning: David tells him that the ark sits in a tent. Nathan says, “Do all that is in your heart.” That night God tells him that David shall not build the house. Nathan tells David that the LORD will build him a house.
people.hadadezer.role: King of Zobah whom David defeats
people.hadadezer.relations: King of Zobah. Syrians of Damascus come to help him. Shophach is his captain.
people.hadadezer.meaning: David defeats him toward Hamath and takes chariots, horsemen, and footmen. David takes his gold shields and much bronze from his cities. Later his captain Shophach leads Syrians against David and dies. His servants then make peace with David and serve him.
people.toi.role: Tou, king of Hamath who greets David
people.toi.relations: Father of Hadoram. Hadadezer had wars with him.
people.toi.meaning: He hears that David has struck Hadadezer’s army. Hadadezer had wars with Tou. He sends his son Hadoram to greet and bless David. Hadoram brings vessels of gold, silver, and bronze.
people.joram-hamath.role: Hadoram, Tou’s son sent to David
people.joram-hamath.relations: Son of Tou king of Hamath.
people.joram-hamath.meaning: His father Tou sends him to greet and bless King David. He brings vessels of gold, silver, and bronze. David dedicates them to the LORD.
people.ahimelech-abiathar.role: Priest who helps divide the priests
people.ahimelech-abiathar.meaning: Verse 18:16 calls him Abimelech and lists him as priest with Zadok. He is of the sons of Ithamar. He helps David and Zadok divide the priests for service. He is present when Shemaiah writes the lots.
people.shavsha.relations: Named with Joab, Zadok, and Benaiah.
people.shavsha.meaning: The list of David’s officials names him as scribe. It tells no story about him.
people.hanun.role: Ammonite king who shames David’s messengers
people.hanun.meaning: His father Nahash dies, and David sends men to comfort him. His princes say the men came to spy. Hanun shaves them, cuts their garments, and sends them away. He then hires chariots and horsemen, and war follows.
people.nahash.role: Ammonite king who was kind to David
people.nahash.relations: King of the children of Ammon. Father of Hanun.
people.nahash.meaning: He dies, and his son reigns in his place. David says that Nahash showed him kindness. So David sends men to comfort Hanun.
people.shophach.relations: Captain of the army of Hadadezer.
people.shophach.meaning: He leads the Syrians who come from beyond the River. David crosses the Jordan and fights them. The Syrians flee, and David kills Shophach.
people.sibbecai.role: Warrior who kills Sippai and leads a division
people.sibbecai.meaning: The list of mighty men names Sibbecai the Hushathite. In the war at Gezer he kills Sippai, of the sons of the giant. The Philistines are subdued. He leads the army division for the eighth month. Samuel gives a different name for the man he kills.
people.elhanan-jair.meaning: He kills Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite. Samuel’s parallel verse uses different names. Chapter 11 names an Elhanan who is the son of Dodo.
people.lahmi.meaning: He is the brother of Goliath the Gittite. Elhanan kills him in a war with the Philistines. Samuel’s parallel verse has different wording.
people.jonathan-shimei.role: David’s nephew who kills a giant at Gath
people.jonathan-shimei.meaning: A man of great stature at Gath has twenty-four fingers and toes. He defies Israel. Jonathan kills him.
people.goliath.relations: Called the Gittite. Brother of Lahmi.
people.goliath.meaning: The chapter names him only as Lahmi’s brother. It calls him Goliath the Gittite. In this verse Elhanan kills Lahmi.
people.gad.role: David’s seer who brings a choice and a command
people.gad.relations: David’s seer. He carries the LORD’s words to David.
people.gad.meaning: The LORD tells him to offer David three things. Gad names them: famine, enemies, or pestilence. Later the angel tells Gad to send David to Ornan’s threshing floor. David goes and builds an altar there. A history of Gad the seer records David’s acts.
people.araunah.role: Ornan, Jebusite owner of the threshing floor
people.araunah.relations: A Jebusite. Father of four sons. He deals with David.
people.araunah.meaning: He is threshing wheat when he sees the angel. David asks to buy the threshing floor. Ornan offers it free, with oxen, wood, and wheat. David pays six hundred shekels of gold and builds an altar.
people.ornan-sons.role: Four unnamed sons who hide from the angel
people.ornan-sons.meaning: They are with Ornan while he threshes wheat. Ornan sees the angel, and they hide.
people.gershom-moses.meaning: He is a son of Moses. His son Shebuel is chief and rules over the treasuries. The list tells no story about him.
people.eliezer-moses.meaning: He is a son of Moses. He has one son, Rehabiah, whose sons are very many. Shelomoth, who keeps the dedicated things, comes from him.
people.shemaiah-scribe.role: Levite who writes down the priests’ lots
people.shemaiah-scribe.meaning: He is a Levite, the son of Nethanel. He writes down the lots for the priests. He does so before the king, the princes, Zadok, and Ahimelech.
people.obed-edom-gatekeeper.role: Head of a family that keeps a gate and storehouse
people.obed-edom-gatekeeper.meaning: He has eight sons, “for God blessed him.” Sixty-two of his family are able men for the service. The lot gives him the south gate and his sons the storehouse. The text does not say if he is the Gittite of chapter 13.
people.meshelemiah.role: Head of a family of gatekeepers
people.meshelemiah.meaning: He is a Korahite, the son of Kore. He has seven sons, and Zechariah is the firstborn. The east gate falls by lot to Shelemiah, another form of his name. Zechariah, a wise counselor, receives the north gate.
people.shelomoth-treasurer.relations: From the family of Eliezer, the son of Moses.
people.shelomoth-treasurer.meaning: He and his brothers are over the treasuries of the dedicated things. David and the captains dedicated plunder to repair the LORD’s house. Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab also dedicated gifts. All of it is under his hand.
people.shebuel-treasurer.relations: Son of Gershom, the son of Moses.
people.shebuel-treasurer.meaning: He is the son of Gershom, the son of Moses. He is chief among Gershom’s sons. He is ruler over the treasuries.
people.abner.role: Son of Ner who dedicated gifts
people.abner.relations: Son of Ner. Named beside Saul among those who dedicated gifts.
people.abner.meaning: He dedicated gifts, and Shelomoth keeps them. The chapter tells nothing more about him.
people.ahithophel.relations: The king’s counselor. Jehoiada and Abiathar come after him.
people.ahithophel.meaning: The list calls him the king’s counselor. After him come Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. The list tells no story about him.
people.hushai.relations: Called the Archite. Named beside Ahithophel.
people.hushai.meaning: The list calls Hushai the Archite the king’s friend. It tells no story about him.
people.obil.meaning: He is over King David’s camels. The list tells no story about him.
people.jaziz.meaning: He is over King David’s flocks. The list tells no story about him.
people.jehiel-treasurer.role: Gershonite who keeps the precious stones
people.jehiel-treasurer.meaning: People who have precious stones give them for the LORD’s house. The stones go into the treasure under Jehiel’s hand.
places.adullam.summary: In chapter 11, three of the thirty chief men go down to David. He is at the cave of Adullam. The Philistines camp in the valley of Rephaim.
places.adullam.limits: The marker shows the general area. The cave’s exact place is not certain.
places.aram.summary: The children of Ammon hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-maacah and nearby lands (chapter 19). Joab and David defeat the Syrians. The Syrians then make peace with David.
places.aram.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.assyria.summary: The king of Assyria carries away Beerah, prince of the Reubenites (chapter 5). He also carries away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
places.assyria.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.babylon.summary: Judah is carried away captive to Babylon for disobedience (chapter 9). Chapter 3 calls Jeconiah “the captive.”
places.babylon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.beersheba.summary: Simeon’s families live at Beersheba until David’s reign (chapter 4). David tells Joab to count Israel from Beersheba to Dan (chapter 21).
places.beersheba.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.beth-horon.summary: Beth Horon is given to Kohath’s families (chapter 6). Sheerah builds Beth Horon the lower and the upper (chapter 7).
places.beth-horon.limits: One marker stands for two towns, the lower and the upper.
places.bethel.summary: Bethel and its towns belong to the children of Joseph (chapter 7).
places.bethel.limits: The site is a proposal. The marker shows the general area.
places.bethlehem.summary: Chapter 2 calls Salma the father of Bethlehem. In chapter 11 a Philistine garrison holds the town. Three mighty men break through and draw water from its well for David. David pours it out to the LORD.
places.bethlehem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.damascus.summary: Syrians of Damascus come to help Hadadezer (chapter 18). David strikes twenty-two thousand of them. He puts garrisons there, and they bring tribute.
places.damascus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.dan.summary: David tells Joab to count Israel from Beersheba to Dan (chapter 21). Dan marks one end of the count.
places.dan.limits: The marker shows the general area in the north.
places.edom.summary: Chapter 1 lists kings who reigned in Edom before Israel had a king. In chapter 18 Abishai strikes eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Garrisons are put in Edom, and all the Edomites serve David.
places.edom.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.gath.summary: Men of Gath kill Ephraim’s sons Ezer and Elead (chapter 7). Men of Aijalon put Gath’s people to flight (chapter 8). David takes Gath and its towns from the Philistines (chapter 18). Jonathan kills a giant there (chapter 20).
places.gath.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gezer.summary: Gezer is given to Kohath’s families (chapter 6). It lies at the west of Joseph’s lands (chapter 7). David strikes the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer (chapter 14). Sibbecai kills Sippai in a war there (chapter 20).
places.gezer.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gibeon.summary: Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lives there with his family (chapters 8 and 9). David strikes the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer (chapter 14). The LORD’s tabernacle and altar stand at the high place there (chapters 16 and 21). Zadok offers burnt offerings there morning and evening.
places.gibeon.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gilboa.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa (chapter 10). Saul and his three sons die there.
places.gilboa.limits: The marker shows the mountain’s general location.
places.gilead.summary: Reuben’s livestock grow in Gilead, and Gad’s families live there (chapter 5). Ramoth in Gilead goes to Merari’s families (chapter 6). In David’s fortieth year, mighty men are found at Jazer of Gilead (chapter 26).
places.gilead.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.hamath.summary: David defeats Hadadezer toward Hamath (chapter 18). Tou king of Hamath sends his son Hadoram with gifts for David.
places.hamath.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.hebron.summary: Six sons are born to David in Hebron (chapter 3). The city goes to Aaron’s sons, and its fields to Caleb (chapter 6). All Israel anoints David king there (chapter 11). Armed men from the tribes come and feast three days (chapter 12).
places.hebron.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.jabesh-gilead.summary: The men of Jabesh Gilead hear what the Philistines did to Saul (chapter 10). They take the bodies of Saul and his sons. They bury the bones under the oak in Jabesh and fast seven days.
places.jabesh-gilead.limits: The marker shows the general area. The exact site is not certain.
places.jericho.summary: Hanun shames David’s messengers (chapter 19). David tells them to stay at Jericho until their beards grow.
places.jericho.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.jerusalem.summary: David takes the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites (chapter 11). He brings the ark into a tent there (chapters 15 and 16). He buys Ornan’s threshing floor and builds an altar (chapter 21). He gathers the leaders there and gives Solomon the temple plans (chapter 28).
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.jordan.summary: Gadites cross the Jordan in flood to join David (chapter 12). David crosses it with all Israel to fight the Syrians (chapter 19).
places.jordan.limits: The text does not say where they crossed. The marker shows the river in general.
places.kiriath-jearim.summary: Chapter 2 calls Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim. In chapter 13 David and all Israel go there for the ark. They bring it out of Abinadab’s house on a new cart. The chapter also calls the town Baalah.
places.kiriath-jearim.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.moab.summary: David defeats Moab (chapter 18). The Moabites become his servants and bring tribute. David dedicates silver and gold from Moab to the LORD.
places.moab.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.rabbah.summary: Joab besieges Rabbah while David stays at Jerusalem (chapter 20). Joab strikes the city and overthrows it. David takes the king’s crown and much plunder.
places.rabbah.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.rephaim.summary: The Philistines camp in the valley of Rephaim (chapter 11). David is in the stronghold then. They raid the valley twice (chapter 14). David asks God each time and defeats them.
places.rephaim.limits: The valley’s exact place is not certain. The marker shows the general area.
places.shechem.summary: Shechem, a city of refuge, is given to Kohath’s families (chapter 6). Shechem and its towns belong to the children of Joseph (chapter 7).
places.shechem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.sidon.summary: The Sidonians and the people of Tyre bring cedar trees to David (chapter 22). He gathers the wood for the LORD’s house.
places.sidon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.tyre.summary: Hiram king of Tyre sends cedar, masons, and carpenters to build David’s house (chapter 14). People of Tyre later bring cedar for the temple (chapter 22).
places.tyre.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.ziklag.summary: Simeon’s families live at Ziklag until David’s reign (chapter 4). David stays there while he hides from Saul (chapter 12). Men of Benjamin and Manasseh join him there.
places.ziklag.limits: The site of Ziklag is not certain. The marker shows a general area.
sources.web.limits: The Bible text alone does not prove its dates, numbers, motives, or how people looked.
sources.atlas.limits: Use the map labels as background. The linked atlas also includes LDS commentary.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Marker positions are estimates for display. A town marker does not prove that an event happened there.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain is a map aid. It does not show ancient shorelines or settlements.
sources.tuell-chronicles.summary: Tuell covers the family lists, David’s temple role, and debates about how the book formed.
sources.tuell-chronicles.limits: This source gives introductory background only. The full list of works and the commentaries it cites were not available. Scholars dispute who wrote the book and when.
sources.luther-chronicles.summary: The overview links the book’s picture of David to worship and a later community’s concerns.
sources.luther-chronicles.limits: This is a scholar’s teaching overview. It is not a separate record of each battle or speech. Its proposed date and priestly author remain unproven ideas.
sources.schaser-chronicles.summary: Schaser discusses music as prophecy and what the book leaves out. He gives options for the adversary in 21:1.
sources.schaser-chronicles.limits: This is one named scholar’s reading. Scholars still debate who the adversary is and how later belief applied the verse. The source gives a wrong Samuel book label. The label was checked against 2 Samuel 24:1.
sources.mcclellan-chronicles.summary: McClellan proposes that Chronicles shows a contest over priestly authority. He warns against reading modern ideas back into it.
sources.mcclellan-chronicles.limits: This is a proposal, not proof of every author’s motive. The machine-made transcript may contain errors. Audio was not checked. Other interview topics are not used here.
sources.wiki-1-chronicles.summary: The opening gives the book’s structure and a list of works to look for.
sources.wiki-1-chronicles.limits: Use this source for background only. The author, the date of writing, and the order of events are not treated as certain. They are checked against scholarship.
sources.cfm-chronicles-context.summary: The article explains that history books choose what to tell. It directly compares Chronicles with Samuel and Kings.
sources.cfm-chronicles-context.limits: Book background, not a weekly lesson on 1 Chronicles alone. Faith lessons and historical comparison stay separate.
chapters.*.mapNote: The points show named towns and wide regions. The family lists do not describe journeys between them.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: No route is drawn for this chapter.
sources.lds-chronicles.limits: This source gives a selected LDS application. Broad claims about later Jewish religion are not adopted. The chart invites comparison, not an assumption that the accounts are identical.
